tests.description: Nothing is genuinely nothing.

tests.description: Several nodes asked about across a session all keep their marks.

tests.description: The state the feature exists to make visible: work scheduled early that tests no assumption. It is reported, never filtered out.

tests.description: The ordinary case: the kind's own label, and nothing else to say.

tests.description: An unknown or unreadable size must not, on its own, make an empty extraction look healthy. This is the half of the detached-buffer bug that IS decidable here: with a zero size the thin-text rule cannot fire, so the empty-text rule has to stand on its own. The other half — that the size is measured BEFORE extraction, since pdfjs transfers the buffer to its worker and detaches it — lives at the call site in briefText.ts and cannot be reached from a pure function. It was verified against the runnin

tests.description: A panel that silently renders nothing is worse than one that renders something ugly: the raw shape is at least debuggable.
tests.key: resultText › falls back to raw JSON when there is no text block

tests.description: Tools answer in the MCP content shape, and the first text block is what an agent would read. Showing anything else would make the panel a paraphrase.
tests.key: resultText › reads the first text block of an MCP response

tests.description: A mixed round counts nodes instead: naming the majority kind would misdescribe what is actually in the row.
tests.key: roundEyebrow › counts nodes rather than questions when the round is mixed

tests.description: A round that is all questions says so — "three questions" is what the person is actually being asked to deal with.
tests.key: roundEyebrow › counts questions when every card in the round is one

tests.description: Once a round opened a phase, the phase is the more useful name for it than its position in the sequence.
tests.key: roundEyebrow › names a round after the phase it opened

tests.description: The first row is the map's subject, and calling it "Round 1 of 4" would describe the idea as though somebody had asked for it.
tests.key: roundEyebrow › names the opening round after the idea rather than numbering it

tests.description: The singular has to be right; "1 questions" is exactly the kind of thing that makes an interface look unfinished.
tests.key: roundEyebrow › uses the singular for a round holding one question

tests.description: An agent turn that writes four nodes is one thing that happened.
tests.key: runLength › extends across consecutive same-kind, same-origin events

tests.description: Notes and answers carry distinct text every time, so collapsing them would throw away the only part worth reading.
tests.key: runLength › never groups a kind that carries its own text

tests.description: The caller advances by the result, so an out-of-range index must not return 0 and spin forever.
tests.key: runLength › returns 1 past the end

tests.description: A run must not span sides — that would credit the person's work to the agent, or the reverse.
tests.key: runLength › stops at a change of side

tests.description: Ids are sequential and a long brief runs past nine, so the transform must not assume a single digit.
tests.key: sectionLabel › handles a multi-digit section number

tests.description: The ordinary case: the storage id becomes the display label.
tests.key: sectionLabel › renders a section id as a section mark

tests.description: Only a LEADING `s` is the prefix. Stripping every `s` would mangle an id that happens to contain another one.
tests.key: sectionLabel › strips only the leading prefix

tests.description: Only a line that ENDS in "?" is being asked of the person; a question mark inside a sentence is usually quoting them back to themselves.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › does not treat a mid-line question mark as a question line

tests.description: A model reply often carries blank lines; rendering them would open gaps in the bubble.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › drops blank lines rather than rendering empty paragraphs

tests.description: Ordinary prose must stay ordinary — over-marking would flatten the distinction that makes questions stand out.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › leaves a statement unmarked

tests.description: A question is what the partner is asking of the person, so it must be detected for the panel to give it weight.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › marks a line ending in a question mark as a question

tests.description: An empty reply must render nothing rather than an empty bubble.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › returns nothing for empty or whitespace-only content

tests.description: The real shape of an assistant reply: a lead-in sentence followed by the two or three questions worth asking.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › splits a multi-line reply and marks only the questions

tests.description: Trailing spaces would otherwise defeat the "?" check and lose a question.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › trims surrounding whitespace on each line

tests.description: One long paragraph is left whole rather than cut mid-sentence.
tests.key: splitIntoSections › does not split a single oversized paragraph

tests.description: A plain-prose brief has no headings at all; it must still come back as a readable handful of passages rather than one enormous block.
tests.key: splitIntoSections › groups paragraphs when the document has no headings

tests.description: A heading with nothing under it is still part of the document's shape — a section the client left empty is worth an agent seeing.
tests.key: splitIntoSections › keeps a heading that has no body under it

tests.description: Prose before the first heading is usually the summary, and must not vanish.
tests.key: splitIntoSections › keeps the text that appears before the first heading

tests.description: A headingless section still needs something to recognise it by, so the opening words stand in for a heading.
tests.key: splitIntoSections › names a headingless section after its opening words

tests.description: Ids are sequential from s1 and carry the matching index.
tests.key: splitIntoSections › numbers sections from s1 in document order

tests.description: The whole design rests on this: no table, so the ids must be reproducible.
tests.key: splitIntoSections › produces identical ids and text on a repeated run

tests.description: charCount describes the section body, so the outline can be trusted without reading any passage.
tests.key: splitIntoSections › reports each section body length

tests.description: "No sections" and "one empty section" are different facts, and an agent should be told the first one plainly.
tests.key: splitIntoSections › returns no sections for an empty document

tests.description: A brief with markdown headings splits on them, one section per heading.
tests.key: splitIntoSections › splits a headed document on its headings

tests.description: Without the id, the model cannot target a node with update_node.
tests.key: summarizeMap › includes each node id in brackets

tests.description: Indentation is how the flat list conveys the tree; without it the model cannot tell a child from a sibling.
tests.key: summarizeMap › indents children beneath their parent

tests.description: Depth must keep increasing so a three-level map does not read as flat.
tests.key: summarizeMap › indents deeper for a grandchild

tests.description: Kind and status tell the model what is settled and what is still open.
tests.key: summarizeMap › names each node kind and status

tests.description: Nodes arrive flat and unordered from the database; every one must appear exactly once regardless of input order.
tests.key: summarizeMap › renders every node exactly once, whatever order they arrive in

tests.description: The model must be told plainly when there is nothing yet, rather than receiving an empty string it might read as a truncation.
tests.key: summarizeMap › says so explicitly when the map is empty

tests.description: The drag threshold is a few pixels in, so the browser may already have selected a character or two before suppression starts.
tests.key: suppressTextSelection › clears any selection the browser already started

tests.description: pointerup can fire more than once in practice; a second restore must not undo a suppression that a later drag has since started.
tests.key: suppressTextSelection › is safe to restore twice

tests.description: The map must be selectable again the moment the drag ends.
tests.key: suppressTextSelection › restores selection when the gesture ends

tests.description: A page that had already set a value must get that value back, not a blank.
tests.key: suppressTextSelection › restores the previous value rather than clearing it

tests.description: The highlight trailing the cursor was the reported complaint; this is the suppression that stops it.
tests.key: suppressTextSelection › turns selection off for the duration of the gesture

tests.description: If a door registers a different set, agents get different capabilities depending on how they connected — the drift this catalog exists to prevent.
tests.key: the shared tool catalog › exposes exactly the tools every front door shares

tests.description: Every door resolves tools through this lookup, and an unknown name must come back empty so the caller can answer rather than crash.
tests.key: the shared tool catalog › finds a tool by name and reports nothing for an unknown one

tests.description: Every tool needs a description the agent can act on — an empty one makes the tool unusable however correct its implementation is.
tests.key: the shared tool catalog › gives every tool a title and a description

tests.description: A page is already scoped to one map, so these two would be meaningless there. They belong to the server doors only.
tests.key: the shared tool catalog › leaves the whole-collection tools out of the shared set

tests.description: An agent decides whether it may call a tool speculatively from this hint. read_brief is one of them: an agent should feel free to call it on any turn, which is the whole reason it answers with an outline by default.
tests.key: the shared tool catalog › marks the three read-only tools as read-only

tests.description: The cap is what stops a confused agent pinning a connection open forever.
tests.key: timeoutMsFrom › caps a timeout longer than the ceiling

tests.description: Most agents will not pass one, so the default is the value that actually governs how long a person has to answer.
tests.key: timeoutMsFrom › falls back to the default when the agent names no timeout

tests.description: A zero or negative wait would make the tool a busy-loop rather than a wait.
tests.key: timeoutMsFrom › floors a zero or negative timeout at one second

tests.description: An agent that knows its own patience should get exactly what it asked for.
tests.key: timeoutMsFrom › uses the agent’s timeout when it is reasonable

tests.description: What a driver or a browser agent lists. It must match the catalog exactly, since a tool missing here is a tool the agent never knows it can call.
tests.key: toolSummaries › summarises every catalog tool with a name, title and description

tests.description: It asks for something rather than only reporting an absence — the point is to get the section dealt with on the agent's next turn.
tests.key: untouchedNoteText › asks the agent to act rather than only reporting the gap

tests.description: It names the section both ways: the mark the person just clicked, and the heading, so the agent can find it without another round trip.
tests.key: untouchedNoteText › names the section by mark and heading

tests.description: The write goes out in the shape the bridge takes: the answer keyed by node id, and the question it belongs to alongside it.
tests.key: useMapAnswers › hands the writer the answer and the question it belongs to

tests.description: A failure on one question must not disturb another that succeeded.
tests.key: useMapAnswers › leaves other answers standing when one write fails

tests.description: An isolated scenario has no exchange to write to. The map must still read correctly; it simply offers no way to answer.
tests.key: useMapAnswers › offers no way to answer when there is no writer

tests.description: The answers already in the log are what a reloaded page shows.
tests.key: useMapAnswers › reads the answers already in the log

tests.description: Editing an answer is posting another one, so the newer value must win on the card as well as in the log.
tests.key: useMapAnswers › replaces an earlier answer with a newer one for the same question

tests.description: With nothing answered, every card is still asking.
tests.key: useMapAnswers › reports no answers for an empty log

tests.description: The optimistic case: the answer is on the card before the write resolves.
tests.key: useMapAnswers › shows an answer immediately, before the write completes

tests.description: The rollback. A failed write must not leave the card claiming an answer that was never recorded.
tests.key: useMapAnswers › takes the answer back off the card when the write fails

tests.description: These three are what the contribution affordances post. Narrowing this set would silently drop a person's contribution on the floor.
tests.key: user-writable event kinds › accepts the three kinds a person can contribute

tests.description: The agent's own kinds are minted by the tools. Accepting one from the browser would let a page forge the other side of the conversation.
tests.key: user-writable event kinds › refuses the kinds only an agent may write

tests.description: A tool whose fields are all optional must accept an omitted payload rather than forcing the agent to send an empty object.
tests.key: validateToolInput › accepts a missing payload for a tool that needs no arguments

tests.description: The happy path returns the parsed input, so defaults and coercions the schema applies are what actually reach the server.
tests.key: validateToolInput › accepts input that fits the tool and hands back the parsed value

tests.description: The message has to name the offending field, or the agent can only guess at what to change.
tests.key: validateToolInput › names the field that did not fit

tests.description: A required field left out is the other common agent mistake.
tests.key: validateToolInput › rejects a call missing a required field

tests.description: The controlled vocabulary is what keeps the map drawable: a kind the map cannot render must never reach the database.
tests.key: validateToolInput › rejects a node kind the map cannot draw

tests.description: The phase drives the nav; one outside the loop would leave the workspace with no step marked active.
tests.key: validateToolInput › rejects a phase outside the loop

tests.description: A name the catalog does not know must come back as an answer, not a throw, or one bad call takes down the whole binding.
tests.key: validateToolInput › rejects a tool the catalog does not define

tests.description: Answering closes the question. Both halves are the same act, and the answer is the half worth a row.
tests.key: visibleEvents › hides the node.updated that an answer closed

tests.description: ask_user writes the question nodes AND announces them. Showing both would report one act twice, and the bare adds are the half nobody can act on.
tests.key: visibleEvents › hides the question nodes that a question.asked announced

tests.description: An open-question node put on the map WITHOUT an ask_user is a real contribution — nothing announced it, so nothing may hide it.
tests.key: visibleEvents › keeps a question node that nothing announced

tests.description: A user update that is not the answer's own close — a relabel, say — is a real edit and is not bookkeeping.
tests.key: visibleEvents › keeps a user update that is not the answer close

tests.description: The suppression is narrow on purpose: an AGENT closing the same node is a separate act by the other side and must still be reported.
tests.key: visibleEvents › keeps an agent update to a node the person answered

tests.description: The whole point of handing the cursor back: re-parking with it must not re-deliver work the agent has already been given.
tests.key: waitForNewMap › does not re-deliver a map through the cursor it handed back

tests.description: The wake path, and the reason the feature exists at all.
tests.key: waitForNewMap › releases when a map is created during the wait

tests.description: hasBrief is what decides read_brief over read_map downstream, so it has to be right for both shapes of map.
tests.key: waitForNewMap › reports whether each map was started from a brief

tests.description: The check-first guarantee: a map created between the agent's last call and this one is already waiting, and a waiter that subscribed before checking would sleep straight through it.
tests.key: waitForNewMap › returns immediately when a map already exists after the cursor

tests.description: One wait can cover several submissions, and creation order is the order an agent should work them in.
tests.key: waitForNewMap › returns several maps in creation order when they arrive together

tests.description: A timeout must RESOLVE and must carry a usable cursor — an agent looping on this sees the empty case far more often than the full one.
tests.key: waitForNewMap › times out cleanly with a usable cursor when nobody starts anything

tests.description: The agent's own writes must not wake it — otherwise an agent that posts a note wakes itself and never actually waits for the person.
tests.key: waitForUserActivity › does not wake on the agent’s own writes

tests.description: An event may already be waiting. A waiter that subscribed before checking would sleep through it and time out with the answer already on disk.
tests.key: waitForUserActivity › returns immediately when the person already acted

tests.description: The timeout must RESOLVE, not hang and not throw. This is the guarantee an earlier unref'd-deadline bug broke: the promise simply never settled.
tests.key: waitForUserActivity › times out cleanly with a resume cursor when nobody acts

tests.description: The wake path: a user write during the wait must be delivered.
tests.key: waitForUserActivity › wakes and returns the user’s events when they act during the wait

tests.description: This is the string every codeyam preview and captured scenario shows. It has to read as an expected condition, not as a failure.
tests.key: webMcpUnavailableReason › names the iframe

tests.description: Each reason names a different fix, so they must not collapse into one generic "unavailable" the person cannot act on.
tests.key: webMcpUnavailableReason › names the insecure context

tests.description: Naming the version requirement is the difference between a person knowing what to do next and assuming the page is broken.
tests.key: webMcpUnavailableReason › names the missing browser agent

tests.description: A bound page must return null, since the UI shows this string only when there is genuinely something wrong to report.
tests.key: webMcpUnavailableReason › reports nothing to explain when the page is bound

tests.description: The security gates are checked before the agent gate, so an insecure page is told to fix that first rather than being sent hunting for a browser.
tests.key: webMcpUnavailableReason › reports the security problem first when several apply
